note: Election of the members retiring by rotation, held on Monday 16 January 1905. Smyth (styled J.P.), John Hughes and Bernard Hughes were old members and Thomas Shields new; "Mr. Shields was the defeated candidate". The Armagh Guardian calls it "the election of four Town Commissioners"; with four candidates and one defeated, three seats were filled. No party labels are printed. Michael Smyth: no party label printed in 1905. At other elections he stood as Nationalist (Keady, Armagh County Council, 28 May 1902, printed 'N.': Banbridge Chronicle, 31 May 1902, p. 3 ("Local Government Elections": Armagh County Council); nominations and labels also in the Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1902, p. 2 ("But Few Contests": county council nominations, with labels); Keady, Armagh County Council, 25 May 1905, printed 'N': Armagh Guardian, 2 June 1905, p. 5 ("Council Elections: 2 Unionist Gains, 1 Nationalist"); candidates in the Armagh Guardian, 28 April 1905, p. 5 ("Nominations: County Councillors"); Keady, Armagh County Council, 27 May 1908, printed 'N.': Northern Whig, 6 June 1908, p. 10 ("Provincial Elections: County Councils: Armagh"); candidates in the Newry Reporter, 2 May 1908, p. 10 ("Armagh County Council": the nominations)).
